language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Hello there, my name is Julia. I am on a fishing trip in the area of Newfoundland with my friend Captain Casey. I caught some fish when I was at sea!
I brought a small cooler and a large cooler to put them in. I put some sea water in both coolers and I placed the small cooler out of the sunlight and the large cooler in the sun.
After a while we went back to shore. When we docked I wanted to get my fish, but something strange happened.

I opened the small cooler to get my fish and I noticed that the sea water was still at the bottom of it. But when I got to the large cooler all the water was gone, but there was a pile of salt left. So the sea water must have evaporated and left the salt! Could this be because I left it in the sun?
When a liquid evaporates from a solution a solid is left behind, but I wonder what caused the water to evaporate in the first place? Can you help me to figure this out?

Julia, evaporation occurs when a liquid turns into a gas. Maybe the sun, wind, or size of the cooler had something to do with the water evaporating? Help Julia understand the factors that effect evaporation.

Now I know all the factors that contributed to the evaporation:
The cooler was large so it had a bigger surface area.
The lid was left open and it was windy, so this helped the water to evaporate.
The cooler was in direct sunlight which heated the water left in the cooler.
Remember: evaporation occurs when a liquid turns into a gas. When that liquid evaporates from a solution a solid is left behind. That's why I found salt at the bottom of the large cooler.
And now that you are an expert in finding causes for evaporation, see if you can figure out which choice would result in the most evaporation.
